text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments in reaction to the release of the Malaysian government's 1997 annual budget, unveiled in parliament by Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Friday.
William Chan, institutional dealer at Seagroatt and Campbell in Kuala Lumpur: "There have been no surprises. In terms of GDP growth, I think it very good because there will be no overheating."
Patrick Tan, economist at HG Asia in Kuala Lumpur: "There have not been too many surprises. GDP growth is within expectations. The trade deficit of 5.2 billion ringgit is good."
Chan Kean Hwa, economist at Jupiter Securities in Kuala Lumpur: "It looks like a social budget taking into account the social consequences on the nation. It looks good for the corporate sector.

P.K. Basu, director of regional economics UBS Sinagpore: "It looks mildly contractionary, with the lack of a corporate tax cut. Especially with a larger budget surplus forecast for 1997, I'm surprised there was no corporate tax cut."

Irene Tan, research manager at Vickers Ballas in Kuala Lumpur: "It is no good. There is no corporate tax cut, and no increase in Employees Provident Fund contributions. It has been boradly disappointing for the stock market."
